prompt: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis? Tell it as a story starting from the US housing boom, include subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response.

plan.title: What Really Caused the 2008 Financial Crisis
plan.description: A short story of the 2008 financial crisis, from the US housing boom to subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response. It shows how many small risks added up to a global shock.

beats.narration: Imagine a bet that everyone believed could not lose. In the 2000s, US house prices kept rising, and lenders handed out subprime mortgages, loans to borrowers who were likely to struggle to repay.

clip_queries: for sale sign in front of house

beats.narration: Banks did not keep those loans. They bundled them into securities and sold them to investors worldwide. This is securitization. Lenders passed on the risk, so careless lending paid off, and risk spread everywhere.

Then house prices stopped rising. Borrowers defaulted, and those securities lost value. Banks feared each other's hidden losses and stopped lending. In September, Lehman Brothers, a major investment bank, collapsed, and panic spread across the world.
Governments stepped in. They rescued banks, injected money, and central banks cut interest rates. It stopped a total meltdown, but the recession was deep, and many people lost homes and jobs.
The real cause was not one villain. It was easy credit, hidden risk, and shared overconfidence. When everyone assumes someone else carries the danger, the danger is still there.

props.text: Risk you cannot see is still risk.
